name: r2-across-2
statement: The RL-Zero-Math delta is small (0.24 % of weight norm) but its function does not lie in the joint sign pattern of many coordinates: it lies in its large entries and in the low-rank magnitude head of each matrix, and its Fisher curvature on the base's own math samples is about that of a random direction of the same norm (leverage near 1). So the effect of an edit is set by where its energy lands, not by its energy divided by a leverage factor. Random-sign or random-direction edits of the same norm give most of the gain on the cued base, magnitude-ranked subsets carry far more than their share, and DARE survives because it preserves the expected magnitude head, not the signs. The model's activations on general text move substantially. The dose curve saturates early and bends down before a = 1, collapsing past it like an SFT delta. DARE tolerance does not depend on the ratio of noise energy to leverage, so there is no cliff at q of 0.01-0.05 %. A large SFT delta (bytegraft, Think-SFT) behaves the same way on all of these tests once its magnitude head is kept.
scope: Olmo-3-1025-7B base vs Olmo-3.1-7B-RL-Zero-Math delta (MLP and full), partial and resampled copies of it, base + a*(RL - base) for a in [0, 1.5], and teacher-forced KL and activation readouts. MATH-500 at the n13 setting (T 0.6 / top-p 0.95, plain) and at T 1.0 with the cue, grader v3. Contrasted with SFT deltas (Bolmo-1B bytegraft, Olmo-3 Think-SFT). Revises r1-surprises-2: the bytegraft result (DARE gives 0/1,200 on an SFT delta that a rank-1 LoRA can fit) shows that sign coherence does not decide DARE tolerance; whether the copy preserves the delta's magnitude head relative to its host does. Does not cover the sampling-temperature results or which behaviours (format, length) the delta encodes.

imports.finding: For Olmo-3-7B RL-Zero deltas, Fisher curvature along the RL direction is close to that of a random same-norm direction; the effect sits in magnitudes and the low-rank head (sign-flip null keeps most, magnitude alignment carries the effect); DARE damage does not follow (1-p)/(p*rho_sign), and SFT-like deltas with low rho_sign survive DARE when their head is kept.
imports.how: Turns the team's flat DARE curve (85.2-87.8 for q = 0.1-3 %) into evidence that noise energy is irrelevant rather than a bound on leverage, and predicts no cliff below q = 0.05 %, a sign-flipped delta near RL level, a sign-only delta near base level, and a random direction far exceeding RL's KL at 30x its norm.

imports.finding: DARE's output error is not bounded by the drop rate or the delta's size; large deltas (MetaMath-7B, mean |delta| 0.017) survive drop rates as readily as small ones once the rescaling keeps their expected magnitudes.
imports.how: Explains why DARE on the 0.24 %-norm RL delta works without appeal to its size, and predicts DARE at 1 % on the 24.8 %-norm Think-SFT delta keeps most of its accuracy.

imports.finding: For an alignment delta the reward is not first-order linear along theta_0 + gamma*delta: it saturates before gamma = 1 and extrapolating past gamma = 1 hurts even when the delta is small.
imports.how: With the RL delta's KL already near its full value from its head and the 0.542 vs 0.549 match only a teacher-forced sum, predicts base + 1.5*(RL - base) collapses like the bytegraft SFT dose curve past 1.1.

explains.how: DARE rescales each kept entry by 1/q, so in expectation it keeps the large-entry magnitude head that carries the function; the added noise energy is simply irrelevant, which is why accuracy is flat whatever its size.

explains.quote: DARE's realized change energy is 33 to 1,000 times the whole delta's
explains.how: Flat accuracy across a 30-fold range of noise energy shows accuracy does not respond to energy at all, so there is no energy threshold and no cliff just below q = 0.1 %.

explains.quote: matched on change energy (two kinds) 58.0-63.8: H_local REFUTED
explains.how: Neuron-level selection cuts across each matrix's singular head, so neither the top nor random neurons keep it; the failure is about which structure is copied, not about magnitude being uninformative.
A random subset closes almost nothing beyond its share while the most-changed 1 % closes 4-6x more, so ranking by weight change does find the special support.

explains.quote: summed first-order scores predict a 0.542-nat drop
explains.how: The first-order sum reaches only 0.542 of 0.708 nats: a quarter of the effect is nonlinear, so the delta is already outside the first-order regime at a = 1 and the dose curve bends.

The two RL runs share the update mask 1.64x above chance, and the function lies in where and how much the weights move, not in signs, so the two deltas share function despite chance-level sign agreement.
Most entries are rounding-level and carry nothing; the function sits in the minority of large entries, not in a coherent sign pattern spread over all coordinates.

explains.quote: the imitation delta (24.8% of norm, 100x larger) does not point along RL
explains.how: Size and direction differ, but both deltas act through their magnitude heads, so size alone does not put the SFT delta in a separate regime for DARE or extrapolation.

At 1B with every entry moved and a 1,000x rescale, the copy destroys the host's interface; this is a host-fragility failure that the RL delta would show equally on a 1B host, not a coherence difference.

explains.quote: Peak at lambda 0.7-0.8, not 1; past 1.1 the model collapses
explains.how: This is the generic shape of a fine-tune delta's dose curve, and the RL delta, which is equally nonlinear in its head, follows it.

explains.quote: the RL change is 11-27x smaller per band
explains.how: Top-50 sets ignore rescaling and shifts in typical activations, so the small change in top contexts hides a broad movement of general-text activations that the delta's curvature, no higher on math than elsewhere, produces everywhere.

Per-neuron correlation and slope are blind to the offset and covariance changes the magnitude head produces; general-text curvature along the delta is as high as on math, so general-text outputs move in proportion.

explains.quote: Mean KL per token after the cue 0.06-0.09 nats
explains.how: With leverage near 1, a random direction of the same norm gives KL of the same order, 0.06-0.09 nats per token; the RL delta's KL is ordinary for its size, not amplified.

conflicts.quote: a random edit of matched norm can give most of an accuracy gain
conflicts.how: On Qwen3.5-0.8B a random edit of matched norm gave most of the gain; the theory holds that the same happens on Olmo at T 1.0 with the cue, where a generic perturbation of this norm shifts the base toward finishing, and must show that the cue base's 27 cap hits leave less room than Qwen's 95 % did.

conflicts.quote: DARE (each MLP delta entry kept with prob q = 0.1-3 %
conflicts.how: With leverage near 1, the noise in DARE at q = 0.1 % should cost hundreds of times the delta's KL, yet accuracy stays at 85.2; the theory must hold that accuracy is blind to KL from noise off the magnitude head, which it has not measured directly.

conflicts.quote: 11.8% of its squared norm sits in 8 singular directions per matrix
conflicts.how: A head holding only 11.8 % of the energy must carry most of the function; if the remaining 88 % of the energy turns out to carry it, the magnitude-head account fails.
Weight-change ranking closes ~5x more than random, but attribution ranking closes 13.7 / 18.6 %, 3x more again, so the largest entries are not the whole carrier and the theory must explain the gap.

rival: Sign-coherent high-leverage delta: the function lies in the joint sign pattern of many coordinates with curvature hundreds to thousands of times that of a random direction, so DARE works because noise along random directions carries 1/leverage of the KL, and fails only when noise energy exceeds leverage. Separation: (1) a sign-only delta, sign(delta) times each matrix's RMS |delta|, which keeps the signs but erases the magnitude head: the rival predicts RL-level accuracy, this theory predicts a fall toward base; (2) DARE at q = 0.01 %: the rival predicts a cliff because the noise energy (~10,000x) exceeds the leverage, while this theory predicts it stays near 85-88 because the expected magnitude head is still kept.

predictions.experiment: DARE on the MLP delta only, keep q = 0.01 % (scale 10,000), attention and norms base, plain prompt, T 0.6 / top-p 0.95, MATH-500 n=500, one sample, cap 16,384, grader v3 (MLP-only arm ~86.4 % under v1)
predictions.refuted_by: 400 or fewer right (a cliff: DARE fails at 10,000x noise energy)

predictions.experiment: Sign-flipped delta: base + |RL - base| with each entry's sign drawn at random (all tensors), opening cue, T 1.0 / top-p 1.0, MATH-500 n=500, cap 16,384, grader v3
predictions.refuted_by: 415 or fewer right (magnitudes without RL's signs carry no gain)

predictions.experiment: Sign-only delta: base + sign(RL - base) * (per-matrix RMS of the nonzero |RL - base| entries), zero entries stay zero, all tensors, opening cue, T 1.0 / top-p 1.0, MATH-500 n=500, cap 16,384, grader v3
predictions.refuted_by: 440 or more right (the signs, not the magnitudes, carry the function)

predictions.experiment: base + 1.5*(RL - base), all tensors, opening cue, T 1.0 / top-p 1.0, MATH-500 n=500, cap 16,384, grader v3: right (with cap hits expected well above 50)
predictions.refuted_by: 435 or more right with at most 50 cap hits (the RL delta stays in the linear regime at 1.5)

predictions.experiment: Random direction per matrix with Frobenius norm 30x that matrix's RL delta: teacher-forced mean KL(edited || base) per token on RL's 500 T 1.0 MATH-500 answers after the cue (RL's own KL to base is 0.06-0.09)
predictions.refuted_by: 0.07 or less (leverage above ~900: the random direction is far weaker than RL's)

predictions.experiment: DARE keep q = 1 % (scale 100) of the Olmo-3-7B-Think-SFT minus base delta on transformer body tensors only (embeddings and lm_head base), plain prompt, T 0.6 / top-p 0.95, MATH-500 n=500, cap 16,384, grader v3
predictions.refuted_by: 100 or fewer right (a large SFT delta does not survive DARE)
